_note: Manual classification of the 400 distinct funds harvested across the Waterloo roster, for real-estate/land-development relevance. Same method as the GBF biotech classification: Form D has no usable sector field, so this is domain-knowledge classification by fund identity, done by one reviewer, not independently verified. Two tiers: land_development_specific (residential land/lot development, homebuilder-adjacent - the closest match to Waterloo's actual pre-committed-lot-takedown strategy) vs real_estate_broad (real estate generally - office, multifamily, industrial, RE debt, RE secondaries - relevant but not this specific niche). Note how thin land_development_specific is: only Crow Holdings Development Opportunities Fund I was confidently identifiable as residential land/development-specific by name alone across all 400 funds - true land-banking specialist GPs (e.g. Walton Global, Land Advisors, Trilogy Real Estate) simply didn't appear as issuers for any of these 14 placement agents in this search, which is itself a signal: land development is a narrow enough niche that a dedicated roster search (rather than reusing GBF's generalist-PE-placement-agent roster) would likely be needed to find true specialists.
